reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown propose the ten sons in Genesis narrowed to the three surviving clan branches Chronicles lists after Benjamin's tribe was devastated in Judges 20.

discrepancy.note: Spinoza cites Rashi conceding Ezra gave the sons of Benjamin different names and a different genealogy than Genesis, from discrepant source material.

quotes.text: Ezra (whom he supposes to be the author of the book of Chronicles) gives different names and a different genealogy to the sons of Benjamin from those which we find in Genesis, and describes most of the Levites differently from Joshua, because he found original discrepancies.
quotes.attr: Benedict de Spinoza (d. 1677), A Theologico-Political Treatise, Part II (1883 Eng. transl.), ch. IX, quoting R. Selomo (Rashi) on 1 Chronicles 8, on Genesis 46:21 and 1 Chronicles 7:6.
